messages:
emily: Heads up — seeing packet loss and lots of retransmits between gpu pods in gpu-slice-prod (us-west-2). p99 token latency spiked around 23:10 UTC. Looks east-west only. Any recent netpol/egress changes?

sanjay: Which namespace + are these only on jumbo MTU nodes? RDMA flows affected? :eyes:

emily: Namespace is gpu-slice-prod. Nodes have MTU 9000. RDMA handshakes intermittently failing (RoCE), and tcpdump shows many ICMP 'fragmentation needed' and MSS drops. Also noticed calico conntrack shows packets dropped by an ipset rule.

kevin: Can you paste the netpol and `ipset list` that are showing up?

emily: Sure — netpol excerpt:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-default
  namespace: gpu-slice-prod
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress: []
```
and we have an ipset named `egress-allow` that should allow intra-cluster traffic. But `ipset list` shows `egress-allow` exists *after* `default-deny-sets` in the chain, and iptables rules reference the earlier set for DROP.

ops-bot: infra-deploy pushed changes to ipset ordering in calico-post-setup at 2025-11-02T23:05:12Z (run id: infra-5478).

kevin: ah that ordering can matter when we use `-m set --match-set` in DROP rules. If the DROP rule runs before the allow check then traffic gets dropped despite the set existing. Also fragmented packets sometimes don't match ipset because of fragmented header fields.

sanjay: Two quick fixes: (1) reorder iptables to run allow matches before deny, or (2) `ipset swap` to move the allow set earlier. Longer term fix: make netpol explicit about allowed peers (namespaceSelector/podSelector) so iptables/ipset ordering doesn't silently bite us.

emily: Trying option 1 now. Running: `sudo iptables -t filter -I FORWARD 1 -m set --match-set egress-allow src -j ACCEPT`

kevin: Good. If that reduces drops, promote a permanent change in calico setup (calico-post-setup script). Also check `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc` — if it's off we might see more ICMP fragmentation-needed handling.

emily: After inserting the rule packet loss dropped to near zero, RDMA handshakes recovered :thumbsup:. p99 latency back within normal range.

infra-deploy: rolled back ipset reorder in infra-5478 and queued follow-up patch: ensure allow-sets are created first and add explicit namespaceSelector netpols for gpu slices.

sanjay: Please open an incident/assignment so we track RCA and test across AZs (some AZs use different CNI config/MTU). Also add a unit test that validates ipset/iptables ordering after bootstrap.

emily: Filed INC-2931. I'll add the test and a short runbook: steps to `ipset swap` or `iptables -I` and how to confirm RoCE flows with `ibv_rc_pingpong`.

kevin: One more note — fragmented packets might not match ipset when match is on src/dst ports. We should avoid ipset rules that rely on layer-4 matching for jumbo frames; prefer L3 allowlists or the native netpol selectors.

emily: Agreed. Follow-ups: (1) update calico-post-setup ordering, (2) amend netpols in gpu-slice-prod to explicit namespaceSelector for platform pods, (3) add monitoring alert if ipset size/order changes.

sanjay: :thumbsup: good catch and quick rollback.

emily: Thanks all — closing thread once runbook + patch are in PR.
